title: Weight-only INT8 profile: integration harness, calibration rehearsal, and guarded regression runbook
creator: Devon Patel
description: Purpose: build an end-to-end validation and integration harness for weight-only INT8 quantization profiles (GPTQ/AWQ) that exercises calibration workflows, synthetic/real prompt regression checks, and automated rollback triggers. Scope includes: 1) a reproducible calibration rehearsal that runs across representative prompt shards and sequence lengths; 2) a lightweight integration harness to validate model variant compatibility with runtime kernel swaps and KV cache semantics; 3) a guarded regression runbook with automated alerting thresholds, golden-answer delta metrics, and an operator-friendly rollback path. Out of scope: re-implementing quantizers or core GPTQ/AWQ algorithms (we'll leverage existing quant libs), long-tail customer dataset sweeps (handled by separate field validation tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Calibration rehearsal: run with standard sample set (5k prompts) and produce per-layer scale/stat snapshots and a calibration summary CSV within the CI artifact bundle
Integration harness: execute a matrix of model sizes (small, base, large), two quant backends (GPTQ, AWQ), and two kernel families and report per-token latency and top-1 answer delta vs FP16 baseline
Regression gating: PR checks fail when pairwise answer delta exceeds configurable epsilon (default 2.5%) on canonical eval set or token-level perplexity regresses by >3%
Canary policy: automated canary for runtime-1.22 that routes 1% traffic to quant variant, collects golden answer deltas, and auto-rolls back to FP16 variant if high-severity regressions are observed
Observability: dashboards created with per-profile telemetry (latency p50/p95, cost per token, answer-delta histogram) and alert rules wired to slack/ops pager
Playbook: documented steps for debug, rerun of calibration rehearsal, and manual forced rollback (with links to scripts and required permissions)
updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Evals, and CI teams. Agreed to reuse calibration tooling from ENG-31741 and to centralize artifacts in s3://redwood-quant/rehearsals/ENG-415000/

2026-03-02: Prototype harness implemented to run AWQ and GPTQ on small model; found a 7% tokenization mismatch where warmup prefixes altered streaming outputs — added normalization step to harness that strips trailing whitespace and normalizes hyphenation

2026-03-05: Design review with PM and Design. Decided to store per-layer scale snapshots as newline-delimited JSONL and to add a sanity check comparing KV-cache eviction behavior between kernel families

2026-03-08: CI integration: added nightly job 'quant-rehearsal-nightly' to run a reduced sweep (500 prompts) on heterogeneous GPU fleet. Early telemetry shows latency p95 increase of 12% for one AWQ kernel on seq_len=2048 — created ENG-422900 for kernel investigation

2026-03-10: Evals feedback: QA observed intermittent answer-flip on prompts containing long numeric sequences when using GPTQ variant on the large model. Reproduced locally; hypothesis: per-layer rounding bias on first attention head. Added deterministic seeding and golden-answer comparator to isolate RNG vs numeric error

2026-03-12: Documentation draft posted at confluence: /quantization/ENG-415000/rehearsal-runbook. Added the initial rollback script and stubbed canary routing config for runtime-1.22. Moving to integrate alert rules with Ops on 2026-03-14
implementation_notes: Key decisions: 1) Use the existing calibration runner but extend export hooks for per-layer numerical snapshots; 2) Add a lightweight input normalization filter to ensure deterministic tokenization between baselines; 3) Use golden-answer pairwise delta with both exact-match and token-level edit distance to avoid false positives from whitespace/formatting differences. Operationally, the harness will run in a separate ephemeral job pool to avoid interfering with production Dedicated capacity. Estimate work split: 40% harness, 30% CI integration, 20% observability, 10% docs/playbook.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: false positives from formatting differences cause noisy alerts. Mitigation: normalization + dual comparator (exact-match then edit-distance) and store diffs in artifacts. Risk: kernel-specific latency regressions block rollouts. Mitigation: include kernel family in telemetry tags and add automated fallback to alternate kernel family or FP16 with circuit-breaker. Risk: drift may be dataset-specific; mitigation: reserve 'field-validation' tickets for customer datasets and mark this ticket as guardrail for canonical workloads.
